properties.decision:
OPEN — Anthony's word needed. Anthony described the role as an attribute of each NODE in an architecture (publish / subscribe / both / non_external). reflow2 already carries something very close: `Interface.designation` (internal | published), with PROVIDES and CONSUMES naming who stands on which side. So the question is whether the pairing role extends the Interface, or becomes a property every node type carries.

ALTERNATIVES WEIGHED. (1) Extend `Interface.designation` — RECOMMENDED. (2) A role property on every node, Anthony's original shape: most general, lets any node participate in a seam; costs correctness, because a Component both publishes and subscribes so the value collapses to `both` and pairs with everything, and it adds a property to 28 node types for a case nothing currently needs. (3) Neither — keep pairing manual as mirror_surface does today and let compose_and_analyse surface a bad seam as an ordinary gap once a human has wired the two sides; cheapest, but leaves exactly the hand-wiring that made this idea worth having.
properties.name: Where the publish/subscribe role lives: on the Interface, or on every node
properties.rationale:
WHY THE INTERFACE. An Interface IS a boundary — it is the one node type whose entire reason for existing is to be the place two things meet, which is exactly what pairs. The publish side already exists there, is already exported by export_surface, and already withholds internals correctly. And a role is not intrinsic to a node: the same Component publishes one contract and subscribes to another, so a single role on the Component would be wrong about half the time. Anthony's `both` value is the tell — it is needed only because the attribute is sitting on the wrong noun. On an Interface, `both` is rare and meaningful (a genuinely bidirectional contract) rather than a shrug.

WHAT MUST BE ADDED WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES, because this is the actual missing half: a way to declare what a design NEEDS from outside — a REQUIRED boundary — standing on its own, without the consumer first having modelled the provider's contract inside its own design. Concretely, a third value alongside `internal` and `published`, plus the matchable KEY Anthony named (an id and a description), which is what one design's `required` is matched against another's `published`. Without a key, pairing falls back to fuzzy name matching alone, and names are exactly what two organisations that never coordinated will have chosen differently.

NOT SETTLED HERE: how a pair is recorded — an edge between the two Interfaces, or mirroring one into the other. MIRRORS already exists for the second; there is no edge type meaning "these two boundaries are the same boundary seen from opposite sides", and adding one WOULD move the version stamp and lock out older reflow2 installs.
